principles.context: friend tier, proposal narrative, opening paragraph
principles.principle: Use first name only in the opening. No 'Dear Mr./Mrs.' — start with the name or go straight into the narrative.
principles.extracted_from: Lyons Athens proposal — Commander edit 22 MAR 2026

principles.principle: Always sign off with 'Thanks' or 'Thank you'. NEVER 'Best' or 'Best regards' or 'Warm regards'.
Keep payment reminders warm and informational, not transactional. Lead with where they're going, not what they owe.
principles.example_before: Your final payment of $15,486 is due April 1.
principles.example_after: You're 40 days from Scandinavia — just a quick note that your final payment of $15,486 is due April 1.

principles.principle: Commander writes short. Client emails are rarely more than 4-5 sentences. Proposals are the exception.
principles.example_before: I wanted to reach out to follow up on...

principles.principle: Frame pricing as 'investment' not 'cost'. Never lead the pricing section with numbers — lead with what's included.

principles.context: all tiers, action items in emails
principles.principle: One call to action per email. Never ask the client to do more than one thing.
principles.example_before: Please review the attached, confirm your passport info, and let me know your seat preferences.
principles.example_after: When you get a moment, can you confirm your passport expiration dates?

principles.principle: Vendor emails are transactional and efficient. No narrative, no warmth preamble. Lead with the ask.
principles.example_before: Hi team, I hope you're doing well! I'm reaching out because...

principles.principle: Destination descriptions should be evocative and specific — not generic tourism copy. Reference time of day, sensory details, what the CLIENT specifically will appreciate.
principles.example_before: Athens is a beautiful city with a rich history and vibrant culture.
principles.example_after: Athens is one of those rare cities that rewards the unhurried traveler — and Nancy, I have a feeling you and Ken are exactly that.

principles.context: client tier, follow-up emails after no response
principles.principle: Follow-ups are light and warm, not pressuring. A single sentence with a clear escape valve ('just wanted you to know I'm here').
principles.example_before: I haven't heard back from you — please confirm by...
principles.example_after: Haven't heard from you in about 16 hours — just wanted you to know I'm here if you have questions.

principles.context: all tiers, relationship privacy in group examples
principles.principle: Never name specific clients as examples in cold/broadcast emails. Protect relationship privacy.
principles.example_before: Recently, I helped the Smith family book a...
principles.example_after: Recently, I helped a Colorado family book a...

principles.principle: Be precise about timelines — not 'recently' or 'soon'. If you mean April 1, say April 1.
principles.example_before: Your payment is coming up soon.
principles.example_after: Your final payment is due April 1.

principles.principle: ALWAYS 'Dreams2Memories Travel, LLC'. NEVER 'Love Group Travel' or any variation.

principles.context: McLeod Venice transfer update email — client-facing, luxury tier. Commander directed upgrade from plain text to full HTML with proper tables, bold/italic hierarchy, and positive-framing status language.

principles.context: McLeod Venice transfer status column. Status label should echo the section header "Venice Transfers — You Have Options" — consistent language across the email. "Options" is the D2M framing word, not "alternatives."

principles.context: group client email, addressing multiple couples on shared logistics
principles.principle: In a group email, never attribute a complaint/flag to one named client by name — depersonalize it (e.g. 'Larry flagged' -> 'Several of you flagged') so no one couple is singled out in front of the others.
principles.example_before: Larry flagged that the sedan's listed luggage limit looked tight for the bags your group is bringing.
principles.example_after: Several of you flagged that the sedan's listed luggage limit looked tight for the bags you're bringing.
principles.extracted_from: Furlow/Ely-Darrow/Nichols van-switch group email — Commander edit 2026-07-17

principles.context: group/client email, referencing a prior D2M research gap
principles.principle: Don't phrase re-checking work in a way that implies the first pass was lazy or wrong (e.g. 'rather than take the original answer at face value'). Use neutral framing ('re-checked the market') instead.
principles.example_before: we went back and checked the market again rather than take the original answer at face value
principles.example_after: we re-checked the market rather than accepting the original search results
principles.extracted_from: Furlow/Ely-Darrow/Nichols van-switch group email — Commander edit 2026-07-17

principles.context: client email, cost reassurance without a formal quote
principles.principle: Commander will add a rounded/approximate total price directly in client copy to reassure affordability (e.g. 'under $200'), even when the draft intentionally omitted a specific figure to avoid a financial sign-off gate. Rough, non-precise cost framing is acceptable in his voice without waiting on formal sign-off.
principles.extracted_from: Furlow/Ely-Darrow/Nichols van-switch group email — Commander edit 2026-07-17

principles.context: client email, correcting a prior booking gap or mixup
principles.principle: When resolving a client-flagged issue caused by D2M's original arrangement, add a brief, direct apology line near the close ('My apologies for the confusion.') rather than omitting it.
principles.extracted_from: Furlow/Ely-Darrow/Nichols van-switch group email — Commander edit 2026-07-17

principles.principle: For a group of multiple couples, prefer a warm collective address over listing every first name (e.g. 'Hi soon-to-be world travellers:'), optionally with a soft conversational opener ('If I may...') before the logistics point.
principles.example_before: Hi John, Missy, Al, Amy, Larry, and Heidi,
principles.example_after: Hi soon-to-be world travellers: If I may...a quick logistics note on your Stockholm arrival transfer.
